feature: Menu rows and buttons are in Title Case
summary: The design rules now say every menu row, menu heading and button is written the Mac way (Apply to Every Cut), and a test fails the build on one that is not. The thirteen buttons and rows that were in sentence case now match.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Pick a layer, turn Key on in Appearance, and read the button beside the colour: Key It Again.
Pick a moving layer, open an easing dropdown in Motion, and read its last row: Draw a Curve...
Draw a curve and read the button that keeps it: Use This Curve.
Pick a cut between two clips and open its transition Type dropdown: the last row reads Hard Cut, like Clip > Transition at Cut > Hard Cut.
Right-click a caption word: the row reads Play from Here.
Open the Sections list at the foot of the panel after hiding a section: Use Automatic for All.

evaluate: Do the panel buttons now read like the menu bar rows that do the same thing?
Is Set What It Is For in the Library (capital For, because it closes 'what it is for') right, or would you rather it were reworded?
Are the labels beside controls (Between the keys, Tolerance) right to stay in sentence case?
rough: The mocks still write rows in sentence case; they are left as drawn, and the rule in UX-PATTERNS §7 says the Mac's casing wins, so audits stop listing it.
Rows macOS writes itself (Select All, Enter Full Screen) were already Title Case and are not read by the test; only rows the app writes are.
The test reads titles out of the source, so a title built at run time (a layer's name, a count) is not checked.
